This first application has been filed by applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.07 of 2024 registered at Police Station Bamori, District Guna (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 376, 376-D, 376(2)(N) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 12.01.2024.
As per the case of prosecution, victim aged around 13 years reported to PS- Bamori that on 08.01.2024, his maternal uncle (relative) Banti proposed to take her to Kaliboat, Fatehgarh.
Her mother permitted her to go with Banti mama.
So, she went to Kaliboat, Fatehgarh.
She stayed there for a day.
On 09.01.2024, they were returning to village Chakri, brother-in-law of Banti mama joined them.
They were returning by motorcycle.

On way, Banti got down from motorcycle and said Banti Bheel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28866119/
1 to her that she may talk to his brother-in-law.

sentences.text: Thereafter, brother-in-law of Banti took her towards nearby forest.
They were roaming in the forest.
Brother-in-law of Banti committed rape on her.
As he was consuming liquor, she ran away and with the help of some unknown person, she called her maternal uncle.
She narrated the incident to her maternal uncle, paternal uncle and her mother and came to report.
On such allegation, PS- Bamori registered FIR at Crime No.07/2024 for offence punishable under Sections 376, 376-D, 376(2)(N) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.
Statement of witnesses were recorded.
Applicant was arrested on 12.01.2024.
He is in custody ever since.
On completion of investigation, Final Report was submitted on 09.02.2024.
Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant has been falsely implicated in this matter.
Referring to statement of victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of CrPC, learned counsel contends that victim had gone along with applicant with permission of her mother.
Applicant was not present at the time of alleged incident of sexual assault.
No allegation with regard to his association or aiding in alleged incident of sexual assault is available.
Therefore, no offence as alleged is made out against the applicant.
Learned counsel further submits that applicant is aged 23 years.
He is labourer by profession.
No criminal antecedent is reported against him.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving his family and home.
There is no likelihood of his tampering with evidence as both the parties relate to same socio-economic status.
Trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
